subject: Octant production: sudden throttles from burst pool misbind
messages:
From: support@octant.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: anna.wu@octant.ai; ops@octant.ai
Date: 2028-09-07T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Production: spike in 5xx and sustained latency — please help

Hi Marissa,

We started seeing a large spike in 5xx errors and median latency jumped from 150ms to ~1.2s around 08:45 PDT. Our ingestion pipeline is getting heavy tail failures and a few endpoints are timeouting. We don't have recent changes on our side.

Attached: traffic_dump_20280907.log (sample request/response traces), screenshot_5xx_spike.png

Can you confirm whether Redwood applied any policy or routing changes this morning? This is impacting our customer-facing flows; connecting ops on this thread.

Thanks,
Anna Wu
Head of SRE, Octant AI
[Attachment: traffic_dump_20280907.log]

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: support@octant.ai
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai; grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-09-07T09:38:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production: spike in 5xx and sustained latency — please help

Anna — thanks for the quick heads-up and attaching the traces. We see the same signals in our ingestion telemetry (error rate increase + request queuing). I'm escalating this to infra immediately — looping in Karthik and Grace for context.

Immediate asks:
- Karthik: can you confirm whether any quota/burst policy rollouts happened in the last 2 hours for the us-west region?
- Grace: please pull any recent routing or autoscaling changes and let us know if traffic was shunted to a capacity-limited pool.

We'll keep this thread updated with actions and a short mitigation plan. Apologies for the impact here.

—Marissa
Director, Customer Success, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: policy_snapshot_20280907.json]

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai; grace_oconnor@redwood.ai; dev_patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-09-07T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Octant production: spike — initial infra triage

Folks — quick summary of what I'm seeing in the control plane:
- At 08:40 PDT an automated rollout touched a new burst-credit allocation for multi-tenant pools (policy id: bp-2028-09-07).
- The policy included a conservative safety valve that quarantines low-priority tenants to a shared "burst" pool when global headroom drops below threshold.
- For reasons still under investigation, Octant's traffic was classified as "low-priority" for the quota handoff (tagging regression in the classifier service).
- The burst pool we hand them to had a per-tenant throttle and a small warm-up window; once traffic spiked it hit the short-term limit and requests were being rate-limited, causing retries and 5xxs upstream.

Immediate recommendation: rollback bp-2028-09-07 to previous config and promote a temporary emergency override that disables the quarantine for Octant until we patch the classifier. Also request a short capacity bump into dedicated pool for the next 24 hours.

I'll start the rollback now and open OPS-1427.

—Karthik
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: [policy_snapshot_20280907.json] (excerpt)]

From: dev_patel@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai; karthik_iyer@redwood.ai; grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-09-07T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Octant production: spike — initial infra triage

Update from runtime team (what I ran and saw):
- Confirmed: classifier tagging service returned an unexpected priority tag for ~92% of Octant requests between 08:38–08:58. Root cause: a recent model refresh changed the threshold for the "enterprise" tag.
- When low-priority tag applied, routing rule RB-guard-3 directed traffic to burst pool B-P01 which has per-tenant soft_qps=120 and warmup 30s. Octant peaked at ~650 qps during the window.
- The burst pool's rejection path returns 429 which, due to our gateway retry behavior, surfaced as 5xxs in the customer's traces.

Mitigation steps taken (completed at 10:45 PDT):
1) Rolled back bp-2028-09-07 to previous burst-credit values.
2) Applied emergency override: removed Octant from quarantine routing and pinned to dedicated pool D-64 for 24 hours.
3) Increased the burst pool soft_qps temporarily to 800 while we validate classifier.

Next actions:
- Patch classifier model and deploy canary with corrected thresholds (ETA 2–4 hours).
- Run a focused test sweep for priority tagging on Octant test harness.
- Draft customer-facing remediation note and postmortem.

Logs and sample traces attached.

—Dev
Runtime Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: traffic_dump_20280907.log]

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: support@octant.ai; anna.wu@octant.ai; ops@octant.ai
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai; dev_patel@redwood.ai; grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-09-07T17:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production: spike in 5xx and sustained latency — please help

Hi Anna / Octant ops team —

Summary and actions taken:
- Root cause: an unintended tagging regression caused your production traffic to be classified as low-priority and routed into a constrained burst pool. That pool hit its soft per-tenant limits during your traffic surge, causing rate-limited requests and elevated retries/5xx.
- Mitigations executed (completed 10:45 PDT): rollback of the new burst policy, emergency override to pin Octant to dedicated capacity (D-64) for 24 hours, and a temporary increase to burst pool quotas while we validate.
- We are patching the classifier and will canary the model in the next 2–4 hours.

What you can expect now:
- Immediate customer impact should be cleared — your error rate and latency metrics should fall back to baseline within minutes. Please share any ongoing anomalies.
- We will provide a concise postmortem and a compensatory package (service credit) for the production impact; I'll follow up with legal/finance to formalize.

Apologies for the outage and thank you for the quick escalation — we will share OPS-1427 and the postmortem link when available.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Success, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: policy_snapshot_20280907.json; screenshot_5xx_spike.png]
